content: The following individuals and organizations contributed to the development of the Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality: First Addendum to the Fourth Edition. These experts represent a wide range of institutions, including government agencies, universities, international organizations, and independent consultancies, and they bring expertise in water quality, public health, environmental science, and related fields. 1. C. Castell-Exner from the German Technical and Scientific Association for Gas and Water, Germany. 2. C. Chaffey from Health Canada, Canada. 3. R.K. Chew, formerly with WHO in Switzerland, now with PUB, the national water agency in Singapore. 4. T.L. Chong, formerly with WHO in the Philippines, now with PUB, Singapore. 5. I. Chorus from the Federal Environment Agency, Germany. 6. T. Clasen from Emory University, USA. 7. L. Coccagna, an independent consultant from Italy. 8. J. Colbourne from the Drinking Water Inspectorate, United Kingdom. 9. J. Cooper from Health Canada, Canada. 10. J. Crump from Cranfield University, United Kingdom. 16. D. Cunliffe from the Department of Health, Australia. 17. F. Dangendorf from the University of Bonn, Germany. 18. L. Endo from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan. 34. S. Enkhtsetseg from the WHO European Centre for Environment and Health, Germany. The guidelines also include a detailed process for managing conflicts of interest (COI). All members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG) and the chemical and microbial working groups (WGs) completed WHO declarations of interest forms. These were reviewed by the secretariat to identify potential conflicts. While some COIs were declared, none required exclusion of any member from their roles. For example: Joanne Brown declared her role as a technical lead on radioactivity in drinking water and remediation within the UK’s Public Health England (PHE). This was reviewed, and no action was required. David Cunliffe declared his employment with a government agency that uses WHO guidelines as a reference. This was reviewed, and no action was required. John Fawell declared providing advice to Coca-Cola Co. on water quality standards and safety planning until 2014, as well as other advisory roles. This was reviewed, and no action was required. Paul Hunter declared receiving honoraria and travel costs from organizations such as Unilever and Suez Environment for attending workshops and conferences. This was reviewed, and no action was required. Shane Snyder declared his role as an expert witness for DuPont in litigation and as a member of expert panels on water reuse. This was reviewed, and no action was required. Mark Sobsey declared being the founder and co-owner of a company producing a test for detecting E. coli in drinking water. This was reviewed, and no action was required.
